extracted.intended_audience: business communication professionals; current and prospective IABC members (NSW chapter / global association)
extracted.subtask_short: IABC code of ethics for communicators
extracted.subtask_description: A professional code of ethics specifying values and required behaviours for business communicators who are IABC members, including obligations around honesty, lawfulness, confidentiality, conflict disclosure, attribution, cultural sensitivity, and professional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent the global profession
rubrics_metrics.description: We represent the global profession: As the only global communication association, we strive to advocate for the profession, represent best practices, define the global standard, and live by a code of ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should act as ambassadors for the communication profession, advocating for best practices and upholding the association's standards in their work and public representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create connection
rubrics_metrics.description: We create connection: We connect business and communication and connect people with communication. We foster community, build special relationships and learn from each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicators should prioritise building relationships, facilitating understanding between stakeholders, and contributing to the professional community through collaboration and knowledge sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace diversity and cultural differences
rubrics_metrics.description: We are a diverse community: We welcome diverse communication professionals of all levels and practices. We embrace diverse viewpoints, encourage conversation and celebrate cultural differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must welcome and respect diverse perspectives and cultural differences, encourage open dialogue, and avoid exclusionary behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on insights and results
rubrics_metrics.description: We focus on insights and results: We position communication as a strategic function that has impact on return-on-investment and demonstrate the business value of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication work should be strategic, evidence-based, and oriented toward measurable business impact and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver on the Global Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: We deliver on the Global Standard in communication through our educational offerings, certification, awards program, resource library, online magazine and annual World Conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should engage with and contribute to the association's standards via continuing education, certification, and adherence to published best-practice resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty (personal integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: I am honest. My actions bring respect for and trust in the communication profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must act honestly in all professional dealings to maintain trust in the profession; honesty is a core ethical baseline for decisions and messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and correction of information
rubrics_metrics.description: I communicate accurate information and promptly correct any errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicators are expected to verify facts before dissemination and to acknowledge and correct mistakes quickly and transparently when they occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obey laws and public policies
rubrics_metrics.description: I obey laws and public policies; if I violate any law or public policy, I act promptly to correct the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must comply with applicable laws and policies in their work and take immediate remedial action if they breach legal or regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect confidential information lawfully
rubrics_metrics.description: I protect confidential information while acting within the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential information must be safeguarded; protection must also conform to legal obligations (e.g., disclosure duties) rather than absolute secrecy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support free speech and open marketplace of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: I support the ideals of free speech, freedom of assembly, and access to an open marketplace of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicators should uphold and respect fundamental democratic ideals and promote open exchange of ideas within legal and ethical bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to cultural values and beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: I am sensitive to others cultural values and beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and conduct should reflect awareness and respect for cultural differences, avoiding insensitive or discriminatory language and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and credit
rubrics_metrics.description: I give credit to others for their work and cite my sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper attribution and citation are required; do not present others' work or ideas as your own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use confidential information for personal benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not use confidential information for personal benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must not exploit privileged or non-public information for private gain, financial or otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undisclosed conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not represent conflicting or competing interests without full disclosure and the written consent of those involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any potential or actual conflicts of interest must be transparently disclosed and, where necessary, consented to in writing by affected parties; undisclosed representation of competing interests is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: No undisclosed gifts or payments
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not accept undisclosed gifts or payments for professional services from anyone other than a client or employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting gifts or payments that are not disclosed and authorised by the client or employer is prohibited; maintain transparency about remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not guarantee unattainable results
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not guarantee results that are beyond my power to deliver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making promises or guarantees about outcomes that cannot be reasonably ensured; set realistic expectations with stakeholders and clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership accountability and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: IABC requires its members to embrace these ethical guidelines in their work and to sign the following statement as part of the application and renewal processes: I have reviewed and understand the IABC Code of Ethics. The association reserves the right to terminate membership for any member found guilty of violating the code, laws and public policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must formally acknowledge the code when joining/renewing. Violations can lead to disciplinary action including membership termination. The code is available for public use with appropriate credit to IABC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted reuse with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The IABC Code of Ethics is freely available to everyone you are welcome to copy it and incorporate all or part of the code into your own personal or corporate policies, with appropriate credit given to IABC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations and individuals may adopt or adapt this code, provided they give appropriate credit to IABC when incorporating it into policies.
